s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and fever following immunotherapy
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
key_facts: 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma
Treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows
Reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various antibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
Immunotherapy was discontinued
Received lascufloxacin and tazobactam/ceftolozane without improvement
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min
Methylprednisolone and prednisolone treatment did not improve symptoms
Bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages
CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy
Cultures of bronchoscopy specimens were negative

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and fever after immunotherapy with ipilimumab and nivolumab

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunotherapy, which increases the risk of opportunistic infections

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to cancer treatment, making him susceptible to viral infections

shortlist.label: Organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with organizing pneumonia, a possible complication of immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's condition progressed to severe respiratory distress, which is a characteristic of ARDS

raw.rationale: The patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and after developing new bilateral infiltrative shadows, fever, and dyspnea, immunotherapy was discontinued, and despite antibiotic treatment, symptoms worsened, which is consistent with immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis, especially given the lack of evidence for infection or malignancy

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: No evidence of Pneumocystis jirovecii infection was mentioned, and the patient's symptoms and treatment response do not align with this diagnosis

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no mention of cytomegalovirus infection, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient has pneumonitis, the specific characteristics and treatment response are more consistent with immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has respiratory distress, the overall clinical picture and the specific findings are more indicative of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
